releases.title: See who edited a file
releases.summary: Edits lists what you saved in the editor and what Marvin wrote, separately.

changes.title: An Edits tab
changes.description: Open Edits to see the latest file saves. Yours are marked as you. Marvin’s writes are marked as Marvin.

releases.title: Pictures open in the room
releases.summary: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, and SVG files show the image instead of a blank editor.

changes.title: Open a picture
changes.description: Click a JPEG or other image in the file list and the picture fills the page.

releases.title: Every file, edited together
releases.summary: The room lists every file. Open one and what you type shows up for everyone else in the room.

changes.title: A shared editor
changes.description: The file list is the whole repo. Open a file to edit it. Keystrokes sync to the other people in the room, and the file on disk updates a moment later. Diff is still there when you want the red and green.

releases.title: Diffs show what changed
releases.summary: Added lines are green and removed lines are red. Code is formatted for the usual languages.

changes.title: Green, red, and formatted code
changes.description: Open a changed file and the additions are green, the deletions are red. TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C, C++, HTML, Markdown, and the other common languages are formatted.

releases.title: The room is a quiet page
releases.summary: Changed files sit in a folder tree on the left. Transcript and Marvin use the rest of the window.

changes.title: Files on the left
changes.description: Open a room and the changes are a folder tree you can search. Transcript is the page, with Marvin beside it. Pick a file to read its diff.

releases.title: Room settings stay with the room
releases.summary: A room’s settings are only about that room. Open rooms stay with Projects. Machine settings sit at the bottom of the sidebar, just above your name.

changes.title: Room settings live in the room
changes.description: Opening a room slides the sidebar away and the room fills the window. The Marvin logo and a back link sit in the room’s top bar. Changes uses the same connected tab as Settings. The sidebar itself is a calmer size.

releases.title: The sidebar is easier to see
releases.summary: Projects and Settings are large rows. The icons, the Marvin mark, and your name are bigger.

changes.title: Bigger navigation
changes.description: The two items in the sidebar use large icons and larger type. Fold the rail and the icons stay big.

releases.title: Settings is easier to read
releases.summary: Type on Settings is larger, and there is more space between the title, the tabs, and each section.

changes.title: More room on the page
changes.description: Headings, descriptions, and controls sit further apart. The row of tabs is larger too.

releases.title: Settings opens from a row of tabs
releases.summary: The Marvin sidebar is the only sidebar. Settings sections sit under the title, and the one you are in is marked on the card.

changes.title: No second sidebar
changes.description: Sign-in, GitHub, coding agents, sessions, and the rest are a row under Settings. The open tab uses the same dark surface as the card, with a teal line along its bottom.

releases.title: The room matches the rest of Marvin
releases.summary: Projects, Settings, and the inside of a project are the same dark theme. Settings cards are no longer white panels on a dark page.

changes.title: One dark canvas
changes.description: The diff, the room bar, the transcript, and the people list use the same dark background as Projects and Settings.

changes.title: Settings cards match the page
changes.description: Cards, fields, and buttons in Settings are dark, with light text. The teal accent stays for the primary action.

releases.title: The transcript reads as a conversation
releases.summary: Each line shows a name, a time, and the words apart from each other. Signing in with an email no longer prints the whole address on every line.

changes.title: A name, then what was said
changes.description: The time sits in its own column. The name is on one line and the words are under it. Someone who keeps talking does not have their name repeated on every line.

changes.title: An email becomes a name
changes.description: maria.santos@acme.com shows as Maria Santos. Hover the name to see the address. The room list uses the same name.

releases.title: Projects and settings are now dark
releases.summary: The join screen, project picker, setup, and settings pages match the Room First dark theme: near-black canvas, dark cards, light text, and teal accents.

changes.title: Dark backgrounds across the shell
changes.description: Projects, join, setup, and settings switched from light backgrounds to the Room First dark palette. Your conversation workspace stays light for now.

changes.title: Teal ready states
changes.description: Ready and ok indicators now use teal (#2dd4bf) instead of green, matching the enterprise calm accent.

releases.title: Talking is transcribed even when no language is set
releases.summary: If this machine does not pin a speech language, Marvin detects it. An empty setting used to drop every line.

changes.title: Blank language still transcribes
changes.description: Leave the language unset to autodetect. Speech shows in the transcript instead of disappearing.

releases.title: A forgotten conversation no longer leaves the room silent
releases.summary: If Marvin cannot reopen last time’s coding-agent conversation, it starts a new one instead of sitting in the room with no agent.

changes.title: Start fresh when the old thread is gone
changes.description: A saved conversation that the agent no longer has (new disk, trimmed history) used to leave the room with a dead agent. Marvin now starts a new conversation and keeps the room usable.

releases.title: A mark for Marvin
releases.summary: Marvin in the sidebar is the gold speech circle and the cream word, with a live pip on the i. Fold the rail and the mark stays.

changes.title: The name you say
changes.description: The sidebar shows the Marvin lockup: speech circle, cream word, gold pip on the i. Fold it and the square mark stays.

changes.title: The same mark on the way in
changes.description: Sign-in uses the lockup. The browser tab uses the square mark.

releases.title: Coding agents lead with Grok
releases.summary: Settings → Coding agents opens on Grok. If that is the only agent you have connected, rooms use it. The default is no longer locked by an environment file.

changes.title: Grok is at the top
changes.description: Sign in with grok.com is the first thing on the page. A signed-in session says so in green. An API key is a secondary paste, not a form waiting next to every vendor.

changes.title: The only agent becomes the default
changes.description: If Grok is the only agent connected, new rooms use Grok. You can still pick another default.

changes.title: Settings picks the default, not .env
changes.description: Claude Code is still the built-in default when nobody is connected. A leftover MARVIN_HARNESS=claude-code line no longer locks the picker.

releases.title: Enterprise settings lock when there is no license
releases.summary: Who may join, company sign-in, audit export, and the GitHub App stay visible but locked until you paste a license.

changes.title: Enterprise cards lock
changes.description: If this machine has no Enterprise license, who may join, company sign-in, and audit export show a lock and dim. Paste a license under Enterprise to edit them.

changes.title: The GitHub App waits on a license
changes.description: Creating a GitHub App for the machine is locked the same way. A pasted token still works.

releases.title: Company name under Marvin
releases.summary: The same sidebar is on every page. A licensed machine shows the company name under Marvin. A chevron beside Marvin folds the rail.

changes.title: The company name under Marvin
changes.description: When this box has a valid Enterprise license, the gold company badge sits under Marvin, on the left. Machines without a license stay just Marvin.

changes.title: A chevron beside Marvin
changes.description: The arrow to the right of Marvin folds the sidebar to icons. This browser still remembers.

changes.title: Sign-in fields have room
changes.description: On Settings → Sign-in, each label sits above its field. The list is no longer one cramped line of words and boxes.

changes.title: GitHub settings use the same fields
changes.description: Client ID, tokens, and the machine / your GitHub blocks on Settings → GitHub use the same spaced fields as Sign-in.

changes.title: Every Settings page is the same card
changes.description: Coding agents, sessions, audit export, Enterprise, and this machine now use the same fields and spacing as Sign-in and GitHub.

changes.title: A license already on the machine is obvious
changes.description: Settings → Enterprise shows the company name, how many seats, and when it ends. The license string is masked. The paste box only appears when there is no key, or when you replace it.

releases.title: One sidebar, and Back from a project
releases.summary: The same sidebar is on every page. Opening a project changes the address, so Back returns you to the list.

changes.title: The same sidebar everywhere
changes.description: Projects, the room, setup, and Settings use one rail: Marvin, Projects, Settings, and your name.

changes.title: A project is a page
changes.description: Opening a project changes the address. The browser Back button, or Projects in the rail, returns you to the list.

changes.title: Collapse the sidebar
changes.description: Fold the rail down to icons when you want more room. This browser remembers.

releases.title: Enterprise mark, and Back from Settings
releases.summary: A licensed machine wears its company name. Settings is a page you can leave with the browser Back button.

changes.title: The company name on the machine
changes.description: When this box has a valid Enterprise license, Marvin shows a gold badge with the company name on the rail.

changes.title: Leave Settings like a page
changes.description: Opening Settings changes the address. Use Back in the header, or the browser Back button, to return to projects or the room. Switching sections does not stack extra history.

releases.title: Company sign-in you can follow
releases.summary: Settings is one page at a time, and Sign-in lists the clicks at your identity provider.

changes.title: One settings page at a time
changes.description: The projects rail has Settings. Inside it, pick Sign-in, GitHub, coding agents, sessions, audit, Enterprise, or this machine.

changes.title: Follow the clicks at your provider
changes.description: Choose Entra, Okta, Google, GitHub, or Keycloak. Copy the redirect URL, then paste the issuer, client id, and secret.

changes.title: Try it on this laptop
changes.description: Local test is a fake company login. Sign in as maria (admin) or alex (participant) without a real tenant.

changes.title: Settings during setup
changes.description: An administrator can open settings to connect sign-in or paste a license before the machine is ready.

releases.title: Finish setup before the workspace
releases.summary: A machine stays on a dedicated setup page until GitHub and a coding agent are connected.

changes.title: Required connections first
changes.description: Connect this machine’s GitHub, then pick a coding agent. Nothing else is reachable until both are done.

changes.title: Waiting if you are not an admin
changes.description: Participants see that the machine is not open yet, instead of a locked projects list.

changes.title: Quiet status after setup
changes.description: Once the machine is ready, GitHub and the coding agent sit as compact status next to projects. Your own GitHub stays optional.

changes.title: License on the setup page
changes.description: If you choose a GitHub App before the workspace is open, paste the Enterprise license on that same step.

changes.title: How to make a GitHub token
changes.description: Paste a token now opens the GitHub page and lists which owner, repos, and permissions to pick.

releases.title: A focused workspace
releases.summary: Projects, machine readiness, and updates now live in one calm workspace.

changes.title: Projects come first
changes.description: Open a project from the main workspace while machine setup stays in a compact status rail.

changes.title: One consistent design
changes.description: Sign-in, projects, rooms, and settings now share the same focused visual system.

changes.title: What changed
changes.description: Read plain-language release notes before you update the machine.

changes.title: Live update progress
changes.description: See each update step and the latest install log while the worker restarts.

changes.title: Clear restart status
changes.description: The room tells you when an update is running instead of showing a raw connection error.

releases.title: Company controls
releases.summary: Connect company identity, review signed sessions, and keep audit copies in systems you control.

changes.title: Company sign-in
changes.description: Connect your identity provider and choose which email domains can enter this machine.

changes.title: Session history
changes.description: Review signed session records and choose how long they stay on the machine.

changes.title: Audit delivery
changes.description: Send session records to your own S3 bucket or webhook.

changes.title: GitHub App
changes.description: Connect repositories with a GitHub App while preserving the person who requested each change.
